subject: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, we want to lock in a concise acceptance checklist so your SREs and our onboarding team have the same definition of "ready for go-live" for observability: dashboards, tracing hooks, error taxonomy alignment, alert routing, and runbooks.

Attached are three items I promised: a short PDF describing recommended trace hook placements (redwood_trace_hooks_v1.pdf), a draft ops runbook (ops-runbook-draft.md) we can iterate on, and a text file with dashboard URLs we'll push to your org (dashboard-links.txt).

High-level proposal (we can refine):
- Dashboard set: session health, token latency P95/99, model fallback rate, KV cache hit ratio, and error-class counts. Acceptance requires dashboards to show real traffic for 48 hours with no missing metrics.
- Tracing: instrument request entry (API gateway), model selection, tokenization, and inference tail. Lightweight spans; prefer sampling at 20% initially, increase for new releases.
- Error taxonomy: map your 5 operational error categories to our taxonomy (client, model, infra, routing, throttling). We should agree on severity and remediation playbooks.
- Alert routing: critical alerts to on-call (PagerDuty), warnings to dev Slack channel + inbox. We'll supply playbook steps for each alert.
- Runbook: single source-of-truth in Drive; ownership moves from Redwood onboarding -> ClearHealth ops after acceptance.

Can you confirm the suggested sampling and the list of dashboards above? Also let me know who should be the primary runbook owner on your side (name + email). If ok, we'll schedule a 60-minute wiring session next Tue to walk engineers through trace hook examples and confirm the alert channels.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_trace_hooks_v1.pdf (18 pages, diagrams), ops-runbook-draft.md (12 kB), dashboard-links.txt

From: Sara Patel <sara@clearhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Thanks Mina —

Looks good at first pass. A few clarifications from our side:
1) Sampling: 20% is fine for now, but for the model-selection span we'd prefer 50% for the first 72 hours after any model change.
2) Dashboards: can you add a metric for "fallback to smaller model" (we saw spikes in prior projects)?
3) Alerting: our PD team wants critical inference-timeouts to page the infra on-call immediately; anything model-degradation (quality) should page product-ops.

Primary runbook owner will be Alex Rivera (alex.rivera@clearhealth.com). He'll join the wiring session.

Can Ben and Laura attend the Tue session? Alex prefers 10:30am PT.

—Sara
Sara Patel
VP Engineering, ClearHealth

> Attachments received and noted

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Perfect — thanks Alex/Sara. 10:30am PT Tue works. Invites coming from my calendar with dial-in.

Notes / updates based on your asks:
- Sampling: we'll set trace sampling to 20% cluster-wide, and add a short-lived sampling policy that increases model-selection spans to 50% for 72 hours after a model change. That's doable; Ben will paste the config snippet below.
- Dashboard: we'll add a "model_fallback_rate" timeseries and a derived tile showing 1h rolling rate.
- Alert routing: we'll make two PD escalation keys available (infra-critical, product-quality). Please share the PD integration key for infra-critical before the session so we can test during wiring.
- Runbook owner: noted Alex as primary. We'll include an acceptance checklist in the runbook that requires 48h of continuous metric availability and no more than 5 critical alerts in a 24h window for green status.

See Ben's config suggestion below and Laura's runbook ownership notes.

Best,
Mina

---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 12:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Alex — quick config snippet for our trace agent (example):

# sampling policy (yaml)
trace_sampling:
  default: 0.20
  policies:
    - name: model_selection_boost
      match: span.name == "model.selection"
      rate: 0.50
      duration: 259200 # 72h in seconds

We'll also add a tag on the model-selection span with model_id and quantization_profile so you can filter fallback behavior by model version. For fallback metric: increment a counter whenever the runtime chooses a lower-cost variant due to capacity/cost rules.

On alerts: we'll send a webhook to your PD infra-critical key for any inference_timeout > 2s at P99 and to product-quality for sustained decline in perplexity/QA metrics.

Happy to demo the tracing hooks in the Tuesday session.

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara@clearhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Adding a couple of operational items for the runbook and escalation matrix:

- Ownership transfer: On acceptance day we will run a "handover checklist" call. Post-call, ownership of the runbook document moves to ClearHealth and we will open a 30-day shadow period where Redwood remains on-call for any unknown regressions.
- Error taxonomy mapping: we've attached an example mapping in the Drive link (see related_links). Please review and confirm mapping of your internal error codes to our five categories. We need that to ensure alerts fire correctly and to populate the dashboard error-class counts.
- Escalation matrix (summary):
  * Sev 1 (inference outage): page infra-critical -> escalate to Redwood SRE after 15m if not acknowledged.
  * Sev 2 (model degradation): page product-quality -> notify product manager and schedule hotfix window.
  * Sev 3 (non-blocking errors): email + slack only.

I'll bring a template for the acceptance signoff at the wire session.

Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@clearhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2029 16:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Trace hooks, dashboard acceptance criteria, and escalation matrix for ClearHealth onboarding

Thanks everyone —

We got the attachments and reviewed. A couple quick items before Tue:
- I'll post the infra-critical PD key to the secure channel (will be available Mon).
- We agree to the 48h metric window, but request a 7-day post-acceptance monitoring report from Redwood summarizing anomalies and any model fallbacks.
- Confirmed attendees: Alex Rivera (owner), Sara Patel, and one of our SREs (Juan Torres).

See you Tue 10:30 PT. I'll validate the Drive permissions for the runbook link tonight.

—Alex
